brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A kuding infusion from Junlian county in Yibin, Sichuan, processed with green tea methods and protected as a geographical indication. Sichuan kuding of this kind comes from Ligustrum robustum, an olive-family plant.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
history: Li Guozhang of Shuangteng town adapted green tea methods to kuding in 1997. Its growth accelerated after the national health ministry agreed that Ligustrum robustum kuding counts as ordinary food. Geographical indication protection dates from 31 December 2010.
processing: Made with a method borrowed from green tea, developed in 1997.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
taste_profile: Slightly bitter with a sweet return.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
